SECONDARY-limit signals were laundered into §4.5 R2 replays. analyzeBatchResponse takes its HTTP-level arm before the throttle arms, so a 502/503/504 carrying a RATE_LIMITED body (classifyGraphql: secondary) reaches runT1's http-failure handler; that handler derived lastClassification from the STATUS alone and recorded 'transient', which evidenceIsRerunnable accepts as R2 evidence — contradicting both plan §4.5 ('secondary-limit signals are not replayable under any category') and evidenceIsRerunnable's own header contract. A partial-data 200 carrying {type:'NOT_FOUND',message:null,path:[...]} therefore resolved its valid aliases and recorded the batch a success, putting malformed transport evidence into the R2 ledger. The null exemption is removed and the parity claim is now true.

AuditDb.open leaked an OPEN writable connection on any post-initialisation failure: the --fresh drop, schema creation, the v2->v4 migrations and the run_unit_head self-heal all run after initWritableConnection returns and before `new AuditDb(db)` exists, with no try/finally — so a throw there stranded the handle and its WAL lock until process exit. initWritableConnection closes on its own failure and openReadOnly closes on its validation failure; this span was the one writable gap between them. This is the 'wrapper fixed, root still broken' class: the continuation loop's round-5 bench guard sweeps the run-cache DB files it named but cannot close a handle it was never handed, and the bench opens one such DB per repetition. NOTE the honest limit: the ownership gate makes post-init failures uncraftable through the public API, so the leak needs a genuine runtime fault (ENOSPC, a damaged page mid-DDL) and carries no unit test — the fix is asserted by symmetry with its two siblings, not by a fixture.

CRITICAL, T1 circuit breaker: the breaker's UnitFailure carried ONLY the last dispatch's evidence, so a mixed streak inherited that dispatch's replay class. {RATE_LIMITED, closed default, status 0} surfaced as bare 'no-response' and bought an UNCONDITIONAL R1 replay — laundering both a secondary-limit signal (§4.5: 'not replayable under any category') and a closed-default condition; ending the same streak on an ordinary 502 bought an R2 replay wherever the ledger allowed it. A sticky streak flag was added. CORRECTION, recorded in place: this entry claimed that flag made a breaker verdict 'never MORE replayable than its least replayable member'. It did NOT — the flag was a BOOLEAN, and R1 (no-response, unconditional) and R2 (transient, ledger-gated) are both admitted but NOT interchangeable, so {transient, transient, status 0} still surfaced as R1 and escaped the ledger gate its two transient members required. All three round-3 reviewers found this independently; round 3 replaces the boolean with a rank and carries the weakest member's own evidence. It keys on the two shapes §4.5's predicate actually admits (R1 no-response, R2 transient) rather than merely on null evidence — keying on null-ness alone would have let one later transient 502 relabel a poisoned streak, the same laundering one step removed. The rule is extracted as a pure exported ranking helper so CI can drive it without a DriverRunContext (runT1 has no test harness); its lockstep with evidenceIsRerunnable is now tested over evidence shapes matching those runT1 builds (CORRECTION, recorded in place: this entry originally named that helper 'replaySafeClassification', which never shipped under that name — round 3 replaced the boolean with `replayRank`, exported from benchGh.ts, and that is the only such export in the tree; the entry also said the lockstep is tested 'over the evidence runT1 actually builds', but those tests construct synthetic evidence objects and rank them directly — neither runT1 nor the REST attempt loop is invoked by them) — the first version of that test asserted a lockstep that does not exist (the predicate keys R1 on the evidence CODE, not the classification) and was corrected, not the code.

fixedInSantaRound3: CRITICAL, found independently by ALL THREE reviewers: round 2's breaker fix conflated the two admitted replay shapes. R1 (no-response) is rerunnable UNCONDITIONALLY; R2 (transient-5xx) is rerunnable ONLY where the §4.5 success ledger carries the request class. Round 2's sticky flag was a BOOLEAN treating both as simply 'safe', and the throw still carried the LAST dispatch's evidence — so {transient 502, transient 502, status 0} surfaced as R1 and bypassed the ledger gate entirely, while the SAME multiset ending on the 502 was correctly refused. Dispatch ORDER alone decided whether a mandated failure received a replacement attempt. Reviewer A (Opus) passed every round while the codex reviewers carried all findings — a PASS is evidence a reviewer found nothing, never that nothing exists. The round-6 fixes, and the code the subsequent prose-accuracy audit produced (the okRequestClasses success-ledger wiring — the ledger had granted §4.5 R2 replays from ATTEMPTED request classes rather than classes with ≥1 successful attempt — the diskReclaimFailed operator log, and the re-audited refresh-evidence disclosures), were subsequently re-reviewed by the follow-on continuation loop recorded in the amendment above, which confirmed and fixed further defects in that tail. Three separate times during the two campaigns, a fix for the gh-exit/fatal-classification family itself re-introduced the table-preemption failure it was fixing (rounds R5-of-campaign-1, audit R4, caught finally at audit R5/R6) — the recurring lesson this file keeps recording: verify the fix against PRODUCTION-REALISTIC inputs, not fixtures the fix's author invents.

amendments.why: A post-ratification review found the harness biased its own primary metric. The §4.6 disk sampler ran a synchronous recursive directory walk on the main thread INSIDE the measured wall, and two further walks sat between the driver's return and wall.stop(). Walk cost scales with entry count, so it taxed checkout-materialising runs (T2a on every unit EXCEPT the api-escaping C3; T0/T1 on the truncated-tree fallback) and barely touched T2c's --no-checkout store — a driver-correlated tax on exactly the axis under test. The §8 pilot could not have surfaced the DRIVER-CORRELATED part: T0-on-C2 creates no checkout, so its run directory stays small and the walk there is cheap — the pilot rows do record sampling (~1.6 MB peaks), so the cost was small, not zero. Fixed by moving the walk to a worker thread and taking the final snapshot with the wall paused (§4.6 items 1 and 4, both amended). This removes the main-thread BLOCKING. It does NOT remove all wall-time interference, because a walk on another thread still competes for CPU and disk bandwidth with the git subprocess under test. Reclamation stays inside the wall on the normal path, unchanged (see the R5 exception noted below).
alsoFixed: the §8 freeze gate trusted `git status --porcelain` without checking its exit code, so a status-specific failure yielded empty stdout and read as a clean tree — the tamper-detection leg failing OPEN

`git rev-parse HEAD` was unchecked and unvalidated, so a failure recorded harnessCommit:"" in every row and reduced the resume guard's revision check to "" !== "", silently merging rows from different harness revisions

the fidelity battery parsed `ls-tree` output without checking its exit code; the deadline path returns empty stdout, which parsed as 'entry absent from the live tree' and wrote a pass:false row — manufacturing a permanent, never-rerunnable driver disqualification (§4.7) from a transient local failure. Local tooling faults now raise a typed BenchOperationalError instead

pinning coerced an absent, opaque, or alias-errored GraphQL response into the positive fact isBinary:true, which deriveRoutes freezes as primary binary-fallback with no permitted alternative — a latent re-pin hazard that would disqualify T1 on an artifact of one flaky alias. Facts now commit per batch, only when every alias is sound

the mid-unit drift restart returned before teardown, leaking the run's sqlite handle and sidecars while its record claimed diskReclaimFailed:false; reclamation is now idempotent and owned by an outer finally that also covers the pre-driver throw paths. NOTE the R5 exception: that path stops the wall before the halt record is appended, so its reclamation happens in the outer finally OUTSIDE the stopped wall — §4.6 item 1's in-wall reclamation applies to the normal path (citation corrected by the post-restack prose audit — the plan has numbered items, not subsections)

the R5 halt record summed httpBodyBytes without the rest-meta exclusion the normal record applies (contradicting an invariant the module states twice), hardcoded diskSamples:0, and zeroed traffic it had actually observed; both records now derive from one summarizeTraffic helper
buildEnvManifest ignored the exit codes of `git --version` and `gh --version`, so a blank version could enter the environment-manifest hash that binds every timed row

BatchChild.dispose()'s verdict — the fatal condition plus git's retained stderr — was discarded by every caller, so a poisoned teardown could accompany a reported success and the double-death message lost the first child's diagnosis
alsoFixedInReviewRound2: the frozen-surface digest walked scripts/ NON-recursively, silently omitting all eight tracked non-test modules under scripts/tui/ — a freeze that covered less than its own description claimed. The traversal is now recursive, which is why the digest differs from the one first recorded for this amendment

the worker-backed disk sampler had no error channel, no reply deadline, and no idempotence, so a worker that died or never replied would hang between the driver returning and the run record being appended; instrumentation failure now degrades the disk fields (cloneObjectStoreBytes null, diskSampleError set) and never eats the row, which also restores R5's before-any-fallible-work guarantee
cloneObjectStoreBytes was computed with the deliberately-tolerant sampling walker, so an unreadable object store could report a plausible 0 — it is a measurement, so a failed walk is now null
parseProbeBatch accepted arrays and non-Blob nodes and coerced absent fields into definite facts; it now requires __typename Blob with correctly-typed fields

BatchChild disposal was only rejected on an explicit protocol fault, and the fidelity path discarded the verdict entirely; the FINAL successful-path disposal in runT2c and the fidelity disposal now both require exit 0 with no fault. SCOPE: the first child's disposal on the respawn path is captured for diagnostics and is NOT itself gated — a replacement child that succeeds still yields a successful run.
alsoFixedInReviewRound3: the round-2 entry above claimed cloneObjectStoreBytes failures became null; that claim was PREMATURE. The wrapper caught throws, but the walker underneath was still the tolerant duBytes, which returns 0 and never throws — so the catch was unreachable and a missing store still recorded a plausible 0. All three reviewers reproduced it independently. There is now a genuinely strict walker (duBytesStrict) that raises on any unreadable entry, selected per-request so sampled peaks stay tolerant and the recorded measurement does not (the post-restack audit later made the FINAL point sample — which folds into the peak and may be a short run's only sample — strict as well; tick samples remain tolerant; see fixedInAuditRound1/2)
the worker's inbound request was cast rather than validated, and reply sequence numbers accepted fractional/negative values; both are now parsed and rejected

concurrent finish() calls raced through one worker — the first terminated it and cleared the second's pending entry without rejecting it. finish() is now single-flight: the in-progress promise is stored before the first await
the awaited walk's deadline timer was unref'd, so a worker terminated mid-finish could let the process exit 0 with no snapshot and no run row; it is now referenced for the life of the request

pilot.json was READ by the freeze gate but excluded from the digest, so its walls, spread, reps, driver, or slot could be edited freely as long as noiseBand still matched. It is now inside the frozen artifact set

diskSampleError was write-only: nothing logged or acted on it, so a degraded disk row could later read as a real measurement. The completed-run record path now emits an explicit operator warning naming the affected row. SCOPE: the invalidated-finalisation path (a post-run rate-limit read failure) copies the same degraded disk fields onto its row and logs only diskReclaimFailed before propagating — that row is already marked invalid for scoring, so the omission is narrow, but the warning is not universal
runT2c's exception path assigned the disposal verdict in its finally and then skipped the check, discarding the diagnosis exactly as before; an unclean teardown now annotates the propagating error
alsoFixedInReviewRound4: the R5 halt path peeked the sampler and threw without ever releasing it — finish() is the only other disposer and that path deliberately never calls it, so the tick timer stayed armed and the worker outlived the run. A synchronous, infallible, idempotent abandon() now runs immediately after the row is durable

the runT2c exception-path teardown annotation was written to Error.message, but the engine records UnitFailure.cause2 — so the disposal diagnosis was preserved in a field nothing reads and remained absent from runs.jsonl. UnitFailure now exposes annotateTeardown(), which updates cause2 (and keeps message consistent)

the T1 fidelity path mapped an http-failure analysis (5xx / no HTTP response / non-JSON-object body — the first two transient-classified; a 200 non-JSON-object deliberately records the terse durable token non-json, outside R2) to route 'unresolved:http-failure' and appended a pass:false row, manufacturing a permanent never-rerunnable driver disqualification from a transport blip. openAndDeliberatelyNotFixed.finding: Any git-transport failure — a spawn TIMEOUT (exit 124) OR a prompt network failure (DNS/TLS/connect/reset, typically exit 128, on clone, scaffolding fetch, or the ls-remote probe) — is thrown as UnitFailure with no HTTP evidence, so the engine records failureEvidence {kind:'unit'} and the matrix rerun predicate (evidenceIsRerunnable, benchContentTransport.ts) refuses it: it accepts only {kind:'http'}. A transient transport failure therefore becomes a permanent, non-rerunnable unit failure — the sixth instance of the transient-becomes-permanent class found in this harness. (SCOPE BROADENED by the post-restack audit: the entry originally described only the timeout subset; the prompt network-error subset is the SAME hole — §4.5's R1 names 'DNS/TLS/connect/reset' as its own examples — and understating a recorded-open defect is itself the kind of false claim this file exists to prevent.)
openAndDeliberatelyNotFixed.CORRECTION: An earlier version of this entry claimed the fix was blocked because '§4.5's R1/R2 rerun predicate and the failure policy are covered by ratified answer 2'. THAT WAS FALSE, and the prose audit caught it. Ratified answer 2 covers 'K=5, the 2 GiB per-unit disk gate, the G4 secondary-limit threshold, and the fixed T1 caps and failure-policy CONSTANTS (§4.4)'. openAndDeliberatelyNotFixed.actualStatus: Fixing this is a §4.5 PLAN AMENDMENT of exactly the same kind as the §4.6 amendments already made in this remediation — not a change to any ratified answer. It is deferred only because the adversarial review loop that would validate it has just run five rounds and closed; introducing an unreviewed change to the rerun predicate now would reintroduce the risk that loop exists to manage. Three of those five rounds found defects introduced while fixing the previous round's.
openAndDeliberatelyNotFixed.recommendedFix: Add a typed {kind:'spawn', timedOut:boolean, op:'clone'|'fetch'|'ls-remote'|'ls-tree'} failureEvidence variant carrying BenchGitResult.timedOut and exitCode, PRESERVING WHICH OPERATION FAILED AND HOW, and admit only the network-facing subset in evidenceIsRerunnable alongside R1's no-response case: clone/fetch/ls-remote failures (timeout or prompt network error) plausibly satisfy R1's 'network-layer error outside any HTTP response'; an ls-tree failure is a purely LOCAL operation and does not, and a process-level timeout does not by itself prove which phase stalled. The amendment must therefore either preserve the operation and admit only the network-facing subset, or explicitly broaden R1 to cover local tooling stalls — an earlier draft of this entry recommended admitting all spawn timeouts, which would have over-broadened R1.
